findings.rationale: Accepted, and correct against the plan's own non-transfer note: a runner-scoped entry would let cursor-grok-4.6-low take an implementer seat on evidence earned by cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast. Phase 5 now admits the pair (runner cursor, model cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast), and any implementer seat naming a different cursor model id is rejected until separately qualified.

Accepted on both halves, and the first half is a genuine design error: the auto guard runs on every dispatch-hetero.sh invocation, so a binary argument or subprocess in the membership predicate would put a live --list-models call and its failure modes on the path of every unrelated dispatch. cursor_enabled_ids and cursor_is_enabled_id are now pure table operations with no binary argument; live inventory access belongs to cursor_model_for alone. The oracle also shadows cursor-agent now - the guard must refuse without dispatching anywhere, including to cursor.

Accepted: Phase 2's prose said the enum moves to Phase 3 while the file map still read as Phase 2. One owner now - the 3b row states Phase 3 and the reason, and Phase 3's itemized list carries the six sites.

Accepted: a single admission test cannot express a contract whose correct behavior differs by recorded outcome. Section 5 now carries an outcome-split matrix in its own test file - before qualification and after a recorded fail, cursor is rejected as implementer; after a recorded pass, only the frozen model is accepted and every other cursor id still rejected; reviewer-class roles and dual occupancy rejected in all three.

Accepted: Phase 4 ran the release gates and Phase 5 could then change shipped resolver code with no gate behind it. The two exit paths are now stated separately - on a recorded fail Phase 4's release is final and Phase 5 adds only evidence; on a recorded pass Phase 5 re-runs CHANGELOG, version bump, mirror parity, contract check, and preflight because it touched code after the previous release.
Accepted - the same model-versus-runner binding gap reached independently, and it is the reason the admitted entry is now a pinned pair rather than a bare runner. Same repair.

Accepted, and checked rather than asserted: at cd3f5f85 engine-scorecard.js's only runner-shaped enum is TRANSCRIPT_PROVIDERS (line 74), used by import-transcripts and not by the KR4 record path, and engine-qualify.sh carries no runner enum at all. The 3b map now records that both were checked and why it matters - the recording step runs after the live spend, where a late rejection would be the most expensive kind.
